lines.text: At 1 a.m., my elevator stopped between six and seven.
Before I touched a thing, Maintenance texted me.
Stay calm, Nora. Don't look at the mirror.
I never saved that contact. Who is Maintenance?
Car 2 is jammed. I can get you moving.
I typed: how do you know my name?
I'm watching you on the camera. You're doing fine.
The camera in the corner had its red light off.
One. Press 2, then 11, then 5.
Two. Hold Close until the lights dim.
Three. Never press the alarm. It resets the car.
Four. Don't step out until you see your number.
Mine's a red nine, painted across from the doors.
The back wall is a mirror. I kept my eyes on the steel doors.
I pressed 2. The car dropped a foot and caught.
I pressed 11. Something on the roof shifted, settling in.
I pressed 5. Behind me, something tapped the mirror. Once.
Don't look. Hold Close.
I held it down until the lights dimmed.
The inspection card had an after-hours number. I texted it.
stuck in car 2. maintenance is watching me on the camera
This is Omar. I'm the only maintenance on call tonight.
What did they tell you to press?
That's the reset code for car 2. Only my office has it.
And car 2's camera has been dead since Tuesday.
Who are you talking to?
Don't answer him. He isn't in the building.
Don't press anything. I'm coming up with the door key. Five minutes.
One of them knew my name. The other had a key.
Then the lights went out.
I typed, where are you? Not delivered. No bars.
And his last text was gone.
He isn't coming. Keep your eyes on the doors.
So why did its texts still come through?
My phone lit the steel doors. In them, I saw the mirror behind me.
I should have seen the back of my head.
I saw my face. Calm. Looking right at me.
I told you not to look.
I typed, Omar? Then, OMAR. Nothing went through.
One bar flickered back. One text got through.
Your texts stopped. Press the alarm. The intercom opens for ten seconds.
Never press the alarm. I pressed it.
Car 2? I can hear you. Talk to me.
Omar, who's been texting me?
I don't know. Listen. I'm on nine, right in front of car 2.
Doors open. Lights on. Nobody's inside. So where are
The line went dead.
You shouldn't have done that.
And the car began to climb. The display stayed on two dashes.
It stopped. The doors slid open.
The wall across from me was blank. No number.
Behind me, something tapped the mirror. Twice.
My phone lit up. Omar's number.
Don't turn around, Nora. Step out.
I never told Omar my name.
